title: Two-frequency correction raised the lowest median spectral weight error in two passive worm models
abstract: We tested a spectral direct-weight score in passive models of two partial adult worm electrical maps. Each model had 180 cells and 90 observed cells. Known unequal independent white source noise allows the imaginary spectral tail to identify reciprocal weights despite hidden cells. We derived exact error for finite proper complex Gaussian spectral samples. Across eight fixed mask and noise settings, the lowest median relative root mean squared error over 33 frequencies was 0.281 and 0.316 at one million samples. A two-frequency correction with the same total samples raised these values to 0.349 and 0.390. It raised the minimum median error at all four tested sample counts. The correction reduced bias faster but increased high-frequency variance by a factor 130/9 at equal total sample count. Generic high-frequency root-error balances are m^(-1/3) for one frequency and m^(-2/5) for the correction; these are not lower bounds on all inference methods. Independent simulations checked the variance formula. Correlated drive gave a positive false weight in a three-cell control. This is a method benchmark, not measured neural activity. Partial anatomy, assumed conductances, known source noise and ideal spectral sampling limit biological use. The bundle contains original code, proofs, aggregate evidence, figures and exact external-input hashes. External records are excluded.
